jobs.description:
This is a new, dedicated Commercial Sales Manager (m/f/d) position created to provide specialized oversight for the Erfurt factory's generator business. The role addresses the need for focused commercial management due to an expanding product portfolio, including electric motors and maritime applications, and increasing complexity in external projects with international clients. To meet these business objectives, the role is structured around three core areas: comprehensive Commercial Offer and Bid Management for all projects, rigorous Sales Process and Financial Governance using tools like Salesforce and PATAC, and proactive Stakeholder and Risk Management to navigate complex international requirements and ensure seamless collaboration between technical and commercial teams. Given the focus on these areas, the ideal candidate will be a subject matter expert with extensive experience in commercial sales and contract management within an industrial manufacturing context. A proven ability to manage complex international projects, including financial calculations and risk mitigation, is essential for success in this role.

How You’ll Make an Impact

- Lead the development and preparation of commercial offers for all internal and external generator, electric motor, and maritime application projects originating from the Erfurt factory.
- Structure, draft, and negotiate complex sales contracts, amendments, and bid documents in collaboration with technical sales, legal, and business management teams.
- Manage the end-to-end bid and proposal process, ensuring all submissions are competitive, compliant, and aligned with strategic business objectives.
- Develop and implement pricing strategies and perform detailed cost calculations for all tenders and proposals.
- Manage all commercial sales activities and pipeline information within Salesforce, ensuring data accuracy and generating regular sales reports.
- Execute and oversee core commercial processes, including the Project Approval and Tender Approval Committee (PATAC) workflow, bond applications, and financial clearances.
- Ensure the fulfillment of contractual financial obligations, coordinating with finance on topics such as invoicing and payment terms.
- Continuously improve commercial sales processes to enhance efficiency and mitigate risks.
- Serve as the primary commercial liaison for key external clients, managing complex requirements related to international tax issues, permanent establishment (PE) setup, and local installation services.
- Collaborate closely with the technical sales team to ensure proposed solutions are commercially viable and to prevent execution problems on complex projects.
- Identify, assess, and mitigate commercial, financial, and contractual risks throughout the entire sales cycle.
- Coach and delegate work to lower-level professionals, acting as a subject matter expert for commercial sales processes.

What You Bring

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Engineering, or a related field.
- Several years of experience in a senior commercial sales, contract management, or bid management role, preferably within the power generation or heavy industrial equipment sector.
- Demonstrated experience managing large, complex international projects and navigating associated tax, legal, and logistical challenges.
- Proficiency with CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce) and financial calculation tools is required.
- German and English fluency.

Rewards/Benefits

- In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme
- We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder
- We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity
- The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose
- In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical

We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.

Roles and Responsibilities:

- Installation, commissioning and sustaining of Kokusai semiconductor manufacturing equipment at customer sites in Dresden and worldwide.
- Maintain a safe working environment and strictly adhere to all safety guidelines, policies and procedures at customer sides.
- Report on schedule performance and take action to resolve any delays, or issues.
- Troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair any issues that occur.
- Being a major part in building and help growing our new team in Dresden.

Skills and Experience that we are looking for:

- Bachelors / master’s degree / Level 6 or equivalent qualification in Mechanical, Electronical or Mechatronic Engineering or Certified Technician.
- Comfortable working on complex electro-mechanical equipment in a cleanroom manufacturing environment, good manual dexterity with a high focus on safety and quality.
- Aptitude to work with electro-mechanical schematics and ladder logic.
- Good communication skills with the ability to work independently as well as the team environment.
- Minimum 2-3 -years equipment maintenance and/or installation experience of semiconductor/pharma/medical or scientific equipment.
- Previous experience of installing or maintaining vertical diffusion furnaces or other semiconductor equipment would be a distinct advantage.
- Working knowledge of MS Office (Excel, PowerPoint).
- Fluent in English and German language and a valid work permit for an EU country is essential.
- Willing to travel to other EU customers and support our affiliate companies in US and Asia.

Research Assistant (PhD position in Renal Research)

to begin in January 2027, running for three years. The position is compensated equal to 65% E 13 TV-L.

The research group of Prof. Dr. Franziska Theilig (Cardiovascular and Renal research) is working on the development and progression of diabetic nephropathy and FSGS as well as the development of hypertension and edema formation as a consequence of kidney diseases.
As a part of our DFG-funded project regarding the impact of epigenetic modifications on preconditioning the diabetic nephropathy, we are seeking for an outstanding and highly motivated candidate for a Research Assistant position to support us. Your responsibilities:

Sample preparation for RNA-, ATAC-, RRB- or ChIP-sequencing and data analysis

Participation in animal experiments, physiological and morphological analyses of conditional knockout mouse models combined with in vitro experimental approaches

Your profile:

Candidates with a Master or Diploma in Bioinformatics, Biomedical Sciences, Biology, Biochemistry, Medicine, Cell or Molecular Biology or a closely related field

Bioinformatic experiences or strong interest in OMIC data evaluation

Programming skills
Basic understanding of mammalian cells, cell culturing, animal experiments and research
Fluency in written as well as spoken English

Good communication skills

Implementing your own ideas while working with an innovative team
Working in a state-of-the-art research facility with a collaborative network in Kiel, other labs in Germany and abroad
Working in a supportive, collegial environment

The university is committed to the employment of severely disabled persons. Therefore, applications from severely disabled persons and persons of equal status will be given preferential consideration if they are suitable.
The campus and the city are characterized by a lively, innovative and international atmosphere. As a family friendly employer, we offer flexible working hours and very good conditions for balancing work and life commitments. We are looking for a scientist to support our Spatial Biology Unit within Technology Research Center to start as soon as possible. We are an interdisciplinary team of scientists, PhD students, and research assistants with diverse background, including cancer biology, neuroscience, and immunology. Our Unit supports projects of TRON, as well as collaborations with industrial and academic partners by providing expertise in histological assays, spatial proteomics, and spatial transcriptomics. We analyze and validate novel biomarkers in spatial context, deepen our understanding of the tumor microenvironment, and investigate the biodistribution and expression of mRNA-based vaccines and other immunotherapeutic modalities. The successful candidate will develop novel methods and analysis pipelines for spatial proteomics and transcriptomics, support projects involving data analysis of multiplex and high-plex immunohistochemistry (IHC) and spatial transcriptomics, contribute to exciting ongoing and novel projects in high-dimensional tumour profiling to translate those findings to clinical settings. The candidate will collaborate with experts across multiple disciplines to advance the projects.
Implement, optimize, and apply robust and reproducible analysis pipelines for spatial omics data
Develop novel multi-modal data integration methods for spatial multi-omics assays
Integrate in-house generated data with publicly available spatial and single-cell atlases
Support and train scientists and PhD students in spatial omics data analysis
Collaborate in multidisciplinary project teams with academic and industrial partners to identify novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets
Review literature for emerging methods, datasets, and discoveries in the field of spatial omics
Present and discuss in internal meetings and international conferences, write R&D reports and scientific publications

Ph.D. degree in a relevant scientific discipline (e.g. Biology, Bioinformatics, Computer Science)
Demonstrated scientific expertise in the analysis of spatial omics data
Good knowledge of cancer biology and immunology
Experience in leading research projects in a multidisciplinary environmentStrong programming skills, particularly in Python and R, with experience in spatial data analysis and machine learning with an emphasize on spatial proteomics
Experience in microscopy image analysis is essential
Flexibility and adaptability to changing projects and organizational priorities
Strong communication skills in English

Enthusiasm and curiosity for the diverse activities of our research institute as well as the ability to work in a team completes your profile.
A dynamic, innovative and creative research environment
An open, collegial and cordial working atmosphere in a respectful corporate culture
A high degree of diversity in the workforce
Access to GPU-accelerated HPC cluster and labs with cutting-edge sequencing and imaging technologies
Performance-related remuneration and other benefits
The opportunity for personalised further training
Job ticket (Deutschlandticket) incl. employer allowance
Bike leasing (Businessbike)
The opportunity for hybrid working

TRON is an internationally recognised institute for application-oriented research. We combine the strengths of academic research with the requirements of quality-controlled industrial developments. At TRON, we share a common mission to develop innovative solutions for the immunotherapeutic treatment of cancer, infectious diseases and other serious diseases with high medical need.

TRON was founded in Mainz in 2010 and works in close cooperation with universities and hospitals as well as with regional, national and international research institutions and pharmaceutical companies.

As part of our team, you have the opportunity to be at the cutting edge of translational science with us.

If all this appeals to you, we look forward to getting to know you.

The Department of Comparative Development and Genetics at the Max Planck Institute for Plant Breeding Research (MPIPZ) in Cologne is seeking to fill

2 x Research Support positions (m/f/d) to contribute to our daily laboratory work on mechanisms underlying plant development and diversity. The successful applicants will work in close collaboration with experienced research technicians and scientists at different levels and they will cultivate and characterize developmental traits in plant strains derived from mutagenesis and wild collections as well as transgenic plants. They will also be involved in generation of new transgenic plants. Experience in molecular biology (genomic DNA extraction, PCR, cloning), and in handling and cultivating plants, as well as experience with plant genetics is essential (further information on our research: https://www.mpipz.mpg.de/tsiantis). Experience working with Arabidopsis, including the generation of transgenic plants and CRISPR/Cas mutants, is a strong asset. Experience with single cell approaches is also of interest. Additional tasks will involve maintaining lab genetic collections, preparing culture media and assisting in organizing and daily running of an S1 lab. The level of independent work and responsibility will depend on qualifications.
Successful candidates will have completed professional training as either a research technician with first professional experience, or as a biology graduate (B.Sc. in plant genetics or an equivalent discipline) with work experience or an additional educational qualification. We are searching for highly motivated candidates with an organized working style and highly developed teamwork skills. Applicants should be enthusiastic about scientific research in an international environment. Excellent documentation skills, computer literacy (Microsoft Office, Electronic lab book applications) as well as fluent English are required.
We offer stimulating and multi-faceted positions (full-time employment) in a friendly and international environment. Payment and benefits are according to the German TVöD and will depend on experience, knowledge and qualifications. The positions are for one year, starting as early as possible and no later than February 2027, with the possibility of renewal.

jobs.description:
PhD Candidate (f/m/x) in Ophthalmic Epidemiology
Code: 1547/2026/5

full-time, 3 years, extension possible
Site: Bonn

The German Center for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) is a globally leading, internationally oriented research institution dedicated to discovering new approaches for the prevention and treatment of neurodegenerative diseases. Conduct research in ophthalmic epidemiology of aging in humans, with a focus on age-related macular degeneration. In particular, we expect you to:

Perform integrative analyses combining multi-omics data with eye imaging data
Contribute to ophthalmic data collection and processing
Contribute to omics data processing, statistical analyses, and the preparation of manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals
Present research findings at national and international conferences
Actively participate in project-related meetings, documentation, and reporting of project progress
Contribute to ongoing projects within the group and develop independent research ideas

A Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field, such as epidemiology, bioinformatics, medicine, biomedical sciences, or a related discipline
A genuine interest in scientific research and quantitative analysis
Strong proficiency in written and spoken English
Statistical knowledge and experience with programming in R
Experience with epidemiological research or large-scale observational studies, particularly involving omics and eye imaging data, including the application of machine learning methods for pattern recognition and predictive modeling is desirable but not a prerequisite
Strong analytical skills, independent and critical thinking, and attention to detail
Flexibility, strong interpersonal skills, and enjoyment of working in an interdisciplinary and international team
Proficiency in written and spoken German

Your role in Cutting-Edge Research

The PhD project will be supervised by Dr. Dr. Petra Larsen, scientific lead of the ophthalmic epidemiology team. The research is embedded in the large population-based Rhineland Study, a comprehensive long-term cohort investigating determinants of brain health. We are seeking an enthusiastic and ambitious early-career researcher (f/m/x) with a strong interest in investigating multi-omic and eye imaging signatures in the context of age-related macular degeneration.

The Ophthalmic Epidemiology research team investigates deep phenotyping of retinal ageing, preclinical changes and disease, as well as the comprehensive assessment of risk factors driving the onset and progression of both preclinical and clinical disease. These include genetic, molecular and environmental factors.

The PhD thesis will focus on the relationship between ageing and age-related macular degeneration and encompass the full breadth of scientific work, including the development and implementation of study protocols, coordination and supervision of data collection, and data analysis and publication.

The project will leverage data from the Rhineland Study, a deeply-phenotyped, large-scale population-based cohort study. Available data include comprehensive multi-omics data, including (epi)genomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, and proteomics; eye imaging data, advanced MRI data as well as extensive behavioral and clinical data, including cognitive and neurological assessments, cardiovascular assessments, medical history, and medication use. The study currently includes over 14,000 individuals, of whom more than 6,000 already have longitudinal data. Additional baseline and follow-up data collection is ongoing.

jobs.description:
Creating knowledge. Making a difference. Shaping the future. This is what the University of Münster stands for as one of the strongest research-oriented universities in Germany and one of the largest employers in the region. Every day, over 7,000 employees devote themselves to cutting-edge research and excellent teaching. We share more than a workplace. We share the desire to make a real impact – regionally and internationally. Our day-to-day work is distinguished by diversity, openness and space to pursue one’s ideas. Become a part of our team – in academia, a technical or manual trade, or administration.

The Molecular Evolution and Sociobiology Group (AG Gadau) at the Institute for Evolution and Biodiversity (IEB) at the University of Münster, Germany, is seeking to fill the position of a

Lecturer

Akademische Rätin/Akademischer Rat auf Zeit
(salary level A 13 LBesO)

commencing on 01 January 2027. We are offering a three-year, fixed-term position (100%) with the option to extend by an additional three years. The prospective candidate is required to teach four hours per week during the semester (4 SWS).

Your tasks:

- Developing an independent, internationally visible and competitive research program in Evolutionary Biology, Molecular Evolution or Chemical Ecology of Hymenoptera
- Participating in teaching (4SWS/semester) of Bachelor/Master/PhD Students with the option of developing own teaching modules.
- Participation in academic self-administration

Our expectations:

- Having fun doing research and teaching in Evolutionary Biology.
- A university degree and a PhD in Biology, or a related field is required.
- Extensive experience in chemical ecology and either of the following two fields: molecular evolution or evolutionary ecology demonstrated by publications in peer reviewed articles is required.
- Excellent command of English is required.
- Postdoctoral research in evolutionary biology, evolutionary ecology, or chemical ecology is an advantage but not necessary.
- Ideally you have willingness and motivation to work closely with students (BS, MS, PhD) in teaching and supervision.
- Applications for Third-Party funding to build an own, sustainable and independent research program in Evolutionary Biology would be welcomed.
- A high level of organizational and communication skills and readiness to collaborate on shared projects within the IEB/AG Gadau

Advantages for you:

- The AG Gadau and the Institute for Evolution and Biodiversity (https://www.uni-muenster.de/Evolution/ (https://www.uni-muenster.de/Evolution/) ) offer a wide range of opportunities for basic research and teaching in various areas of evolutionary biology, evolutionary ecology, bioinformatics, and biodiversity research.
- The international and interdisciplinary teams at the IEB and within the AG Gadau foster a collaborative working environment and are actively involved in numerous national and international research. This creates ideal conditions for collaborations within these consortia as well as for independent research projects.
-  Appreciation, commitment, openness and respect – values which are important to us.
- Our broad range of diverse work-time models offers great flexibility – also when working from home.
- If you have family members or young children in your care, our Family Service Office offers concrete support to help you balance your private and professional responsibilities.
- As an educational institution, we are deeply committed to offering occupational training and continuing education opportunities tailored to your individual needs.
- From A – Z, Aikido to Zumba, our sport and health programmes ensure a healthy work-life balance.

The University of Münster strongly supports equal opportunity and diversity (https://www.uni-muenster.de/profil/en/diversity/policy/mission-statement.html) . We welcome all applicants regardless of sex, nationality, ethnic or social background, religion or worldview, disability, age, sexual orientation or gender identity. We are committed to creating family-friendly working conditions.

We actively encourage applications by women. Women with equivalent qualifications and academic achievements will be preferentially considered unless these are outweighed by reasons which necessitate the selection of another candidate.

If you have any questions, please contact Prof. Jürgen Gadau (gadauj@uni-muenster.de (gadauj@uni-muenster.de) ) or Dr. Lukas Schrader (lukas.schrader@uni-muenster.de (lukas.schrader@uni-muenster.de) ).

Are you interested? Then we look forward to receiving your application (CV and 2-3-page description of your research plan) by 28-10-2026 exclusively via our online application portal.

For sustainability reasons, we kindly ask you to refrain from submitting paper/printed documents.

Prof. Dr. Jürgen Gadau
Faculty of Biology
Institute for Evolution and Biodiversity

48149 Münster

Postdocs (2 years) (m,f,x)

The Cluster of Excellence "CASA: Securing the Digital Society" is funded by DFG for the years 2026-2032 with approximately 53 million euros. CASA aims to strengthen the resilience of our digital society. The emergence of disruptive technologies in recent years, especially artificial intelligence and quantum computers, has caused substantial new challenges for cybersecurity research. In the second funding phase, CASA will specifically address these challenges. Thematic priorities include the security of quantum technologies, protection against Al-based disinformation and societal polarization, and new approaches to defending against ransomware. In addition to technical questions, it also investigates the interaction of human behavior and cybersecurity. Research at CASA, which is based at the Horst Görtz Institute for IT Security, follows a strongly interdisciplinary approach. Researchers from the fields of computerscience, cryptography, electrical engineering, mathematics, and psychology work together in an unique constellation in Europe. This holistic approach is unparalleled and holds the potential for scientific breakthroughs. Ruhr-University Bochum (RUB) and its Faculty of Computer Science offer an excellent environment for aspiring young researchers. 20 years ago, the Horst Görtz Institute for IT Security (HGI) was founded here. lt is now one of Europe's most prestigious institutions for basic computer security research. The HGI maintains extensive networks with leading research institutions worldwide and with media and industry. Moreover, it has produced numerous successful security startups. The pioneering work of the HGI forms the basis for the Cluster of Excellence CASA.

jobs.occupation: Senior Principal Scientist (all genders) - Quantum Mechanics and Modeling (Ingenieur/in - Chemietechnik)
jobs.description:
At Bayer we’re visionaries, driven to solve the world’s toughest challenges and striving for a world where ,Health for all, Hunger for none’ is no longer a dream, but a real possibility. We’re doing it with energy, curiosity and sheer dedication, always learning from unique perspectives of those around us, expanding our thinking, growing our capabilities and redefining ‘impossible’. There are so many reasons to join us. If you’re hungry to build a varied and meaningful career in a community of brilliant and diverse minds to make a real difference, there’s only one choice.

Senior Principal Scientist (all genders) - Quantum Mechanics and Modeling

As a key player in our R&D digital transformation, you will leverage quantum mechanics, physics-based modeling, machine learning and AI to predict molecular properties, design and prioritize compounds across our discovery portfolio. Collaborating closely with medicinal chemists, structural biologists, biologists, and data engineers, you will drive discovery project milestones and advance our digital transformation in R&D. Your role is crucial in shaping the future of drug discovery and development through innovative digital solutions.

YOUR TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

- You advance drug discovery projects using quantum mechanics, data science, and modeling approaches to enable data‑driven decision‑making.
- You enable AI‑augmented Design‑Make‑Test‑Analyze cycles by advancing and applying methods for in‑silico compound design and characterization.
- 
Applying cutting‑edge quantum mechanics methods to advance drug development and to generate a deep understanding of molecular interactions is central to your function

- You collaborate closely with experimentalists and internal partners to identify scientific challenges and develop effective solutions.
- You lead strategic digital initiatives and actively co‑shape the R&D digital strategy.
- Working closely with the Data Science & AI unit to leverage next‑generation technologies and drive the adoption of digital solutions is a core part of your role
- You share your skills and knowledge by coaching and teaching others, demonstrating collaborative and supportive behaviors.
- You contribute to self‑directed teams that work collaboratively and align with Bayer’s leadership standards.

WHO YOU ARE

- You hold a PhD in quantum chemistry, computational chemistry, chemistry, computer science, or a related discipline, with strong knowledge of organic chemistry.
- Demonstrated success in an industry setting defines your professional track record, supported by extensive professional experience where you have utilized a diverse range of ligand‑ and structure‑based approaches, including virtual screening, docking, molecular dynamics, binding‑affinity calculations, generative design approaches, and holistic workflows
- You are proficient in quantum mechanics software such as ORCA and xTB, and you have experience in scripting, programming, and workflow automation
- You have experience working with AI‑driven DMTA loops in a pharmaceutical setting, as well as practical exposure to computational workflows that integrate AI, modeling, and chemistry
- You demonstrate high interest in managing high‑performance infrastructure and working with external IT providers
- You emb  holistic health principles and align your work with the organization’s vision as part of Bayer.
- Curiosity, creativity, and a strong passion for drug discovery are central characteristics that define you
- Fluency in English (written and spoken), with strong communication skills and the ability to present complex data clearly and effectively, round off your profile

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

This position can be filled on a full-time or near full-time (min. 80%) basis.

WHAT WE OFFER

Our benefits package is flexible, appreciative, and tailored to your lifestyle, because: What matters to you, matters to us!

- We ensure your financial stability with a competitive salary between 109.800€ and 138.500€ per year (full-time) plus a variable component and a global equity-based cash plan. Your compensation is based on your qualifications, skills, and professional experience.
- Whether it’s hybrid work models or part-time arrangements: Whenever it is possible, you will have the flexibility to work how, when and where it is best for you.
- Your family is a top priority. We offer loving company daycare centers at multiple locations, support in finding childcare, time off for the care of elderly or dependent family members, summer camps for children, and much more.
- We support your professional growth by providing access to learning and development opportunities, training programs through the Bayer Learning Academy, development dialogues, as well as coaching and mentoring programs.
- We promote health awareness and opportunities for selfcare through various measures, such as free health checks with the company doctor.
- We emb  diversity by providing an inclusive work environment in which you are welcomed, supported, and encouraged to bring your whole self to work.

Be You. Be Bayer.
